facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Marshosaurus to be 4.5 meters long and weigh 200 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 4.5 m and its weight at 200 kg.

facts.statement: The holotype ilium of Marshosaurus measures 37.5 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The holotype ilium has a length of 37.5 cm.

facts.statement: If the cranial material belongs to Marshosaurus, the skull would be approximately 60 centimeters long.
facts.quote: If the cranial material is correctly referred, the skull was about 60 cm long.

facts.statement: Matthew Carrano identified a unique trait of Marshosaurus where the suture between the pubic peduncle and pubic bone is convex at the front and concave at the rear.
facts.quote: In 2012, Matthew Carrano established one autapomorphy, a unique derived trait of the holotype: the suture between the pubic peduncle and the pubic bone is convex, curving upwards, at the front and concave at the rear.

facts.statement: James Henry Madsen Jr. named the type species Marshosaurus bicentesimus in 1976.
facts.quote: In 1976 the second was by Madsen named as the type species Marshosaurus bicentesimus.

facts.statement: The genus name Marshosaurus honors paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh.
facts.quote: The generic name honoured the nineteenth century paleontologist Professor Othniel Charles Marsh, who described many dinosaur fossils during the Bone Wars.

facts.statement: The specific name bicentesimus was chosen to honor the bicentennial of the United States of America.
facts.quote: The specific name was chosen "in honor of the bicentennial of the United States of America".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation dating to approximately 155 to 152 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype, UMNH VP 6373, was found in a layer of the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation dating from the late Kimmeridgian, approximately 155 - 152 mya.

facts.statement: The known fossil material represents at least three individuals of Marshosaurus.
facts.quote: The material represents at least three individuals.

facts.statement: Marshosaurus lived in the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of Utah and possibly Colorado.
facts.quote: Marshosaurus is a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur, belonging to the family Piatnitzkysauridae, from the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of Utah and possibly Colorado.

facts.statement: The Morrison Formation, where Marshosaurus fossils are found, dates from the late Oxfordian to early Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: The Morrison Formation is a sequence of shallow marine and alluvial sediments which, according to radiometric dating, ranges between 156.3 million years old (Ma) at its base, to 146.8 million years old at the top, which places it in the late Oxfordian, Kimmeridgian, and early Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic period.

facts.statement: The environment of the Morrison Formation is interpreted as semiarid with distinct wet and dry seasons.
facts.quote: This formation is interpreted as a semiarid environment with distinct wet and dry seasons.

facts.statement: Roger Benson classified Marshosaurus as a megalosauroid in a 2010 phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: However, Roger Benson (2010) found it to be a megalosauroid in a phylogenetic analysis of Megalosaurus and 40 other theropods.

facts.statement: One right ilium of Marshosaurus bicentesimus shows deformation likely caused by injury.
facts.quote: One right ilium of a Marshosaurus bicentesimus is deformed by "an undescribed pathology" which probably originated as a consequence of injury.

facts.statement: Another Marshosaurus specimen possesses a pathological rib.
facts.quote: Another specimen has a pathological rib.

facts.statement: A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild found no signs of stress fractures in five foot bones referred to Marshosaurus.
facts.quote: In a 2001 study conducted by Bruce Rothschild and other paleontologists, five foot bones referred to Marshosaurus were examined for signs of stress fracture, but none were found.

facts.statement: James Henry Madsen originally placed the phylogenetic position of Marshosaurus as uncertain within Theropoda.
facts.quote: Madsen originally was unsure about the phylogenetic position of Marshosaurus, placing it as Theropoda incertae sedis.

facts.statement: Marshosaurus is classified as a member of the family Piatnitzkysauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Piatnitzkysauridae

facts.statement: Marshosaurus belongs to the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Marshosaurus lived between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Morrison Formation, where Marshosaurus fossils were found, became the center of the Bone Wars in 1877 between paleontologists Othniel Charles Marsh and Edward Drinker Cope.
facts.quote: En 1877, esta formación se convirtió en el centro de Las Guerras de los Huesos, una rivalidad de recolección de fósiles entre los primeros paleontólogos Othniel Charles Marsh y Edward Drinker Cope.

facts.statement: A right ilium of a Marshosaurus bicentesimus shows deformation likely caused by an injury, representing evidence of a pathology.
facts.quote: Un ilion derecho de un Marshosaurus bicentesimus está deformado por "una patología no descrita" que probablemente se originó como consecuencia de una lesión.

facts.statement: A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild and others examined five Marshosaurus foot bones for stress fractures but found none.
facts.quote: En un estudio de 2001 realizado por Bruce Rothschild y otros paleontólogos, se examinaron los huesos de cinco pies referidos a Marshosaurus en busca de signos de fractura por estrés , pero no se encontró ninguno.

facts.statement: The Morrison Formation, dating from 156.3 to 146.8 million years ago, represents a Late Jurassic environment ranging from the Oxfordian to early Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: La Formación Morrison es una secuencia de sedimentos marinos y aluviales poco profundos que, según la datación radiométrica , oscila entre 156,3 millones de años en su base, a 146,8 millones de años en la parte superior, lo que la coloca a finales de Oxfordiense, Kimmeridgiense, y las primeras etapas de Titoniense del período Jurásico Tardío.

facts.statement: The Morrison Formation is interpreted as a semi-arid environment with distinct wet and dry seasons.
facts.quote: Esta formación se interpreta como un ambiente semiárido con distintas estaciones húmedas y secas.

facts.statement: The Morrison Basin, inhabited by dinosaurs including Marshosaurus, extended from New Mexico to Alberta and Saskatchewan.
facts.quote: La cuenca de Morrison, donde vivían los dinosaurios, se extendía desde Nuevo México hasta Alberta y Saskatchewan

facts.statement: Sediments in the Morrison Basin were transported by streams and rivers and deposited in swamps, lakes, river channels, and floodplains.
facts.quote: Los depósitos de sus cuencas de drenaje orientadas al este fueron transportados por arroyos y ríos y se depositaron en tierras bajas pantanosas, lagos, canales de ríos y llanuras de inundación.

facts.statement: The Morrison Formation environment was dominated by giant sauropod dinosaurs such as Camarasaurus, Brachiosaurus, Barosaurus, Diplodocus, and Apatosaurus.
facts.quote: La Formación Morrison registra un entorno y un tiempo dominado por gigantescos dinosaurios saurópodos como Camarasaurus , Brachiosaurus, Barosaurus, Diplodocus y Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: Marshosaurus lived alongside ornithischian herbivores including Camptosaurus, Dryosaurus, Stegosaurus, and Othnielosaurus.
facts.quote: Los dinosaurios que vivieron junto a Marshosaurus incluyen a los herbívoros ornitisquios Camptosaurus, Dryosaurus, Stegosaurus y Othnielosaurus.

facts.statement: Predators in the Marshosaurus paleoenvironment included theropods such as Saurophaganax, Torvosaurus, Ceratosaurus, Stokesosaurus, Ornitholestes, and Allosaurus.
facts.quote: Los depredadores en este paleoambiente incluyeron los terópodos Saurophaganax , Torvosaurus , Ceratosaurus, Stokesosaurus, Ornitholestes y Allosaurus

facts.statement: Early mammals, including docodonts, multituberculates, symmetrodonts, and triconodonts, were present in the region.
facts.quote: Los primeros mamíferos estuvieron presentes en esta región, como docodontes, multituberculados, simétrodontes y triconodontos.

facts.statement: The flora of the time included green algae, fungi, mosses, horsetails, cycads, ginkgos, and various conifer families.
facts.quote: La flora de la época ha sido revelada por fósiles de algas verdes, hongos y musgos, colas de caballo, cícadas, ginkgos y varias familias de coníferas.

facts.statement: Vegetation in the area ranged from riverbank forests of ferns and tree ferns to fern savannas with occasional trees like the araucaria Brachyphyllum.
facts.quote: La vegetación varía de bosques en galería al borde de los ríos de helechos y helechos arborescentes, a sabanas de helechos con árboles ocasionales, tales como la araucaria Brachyphyllum.
